a Mac. Expo compiles the Swift/CoreBluetooth module on their macOS runners.
This is the whole reason a paid Apple Developer account was needed: EAS can
build for a free account, but INSTALLING on a physical iPhone needs signing
credentials (ad-hoc provisioning or App Store distribution) that Apple only
production → TestFlight. Slower per round (App Store Connect processing),
but no UDID registration and it survives 1 year, not 7 days.
preview    → straight onto the phone by QR. Fastest loop for hardware work;
needs the iPhone's UDID registered once (eas device:create).
development→ dev client + Metro, for stepping through JS against real BLE.
⚠️ appVersion/buildNumber: TestFlight REFUSES a build number it has already
seen, so it is auto-incremented remotely rather than by hand — a rejected
upload after a 20-minute build is a bad way to learn that.
